the structure-function relationship and molecular interactions of the virulence factor PsrP.

the BR of PsrP adopts an unusual MSCRAMM fold, which is a variant of the DE-IgG fold.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined a novel structure of a microbial surface adhesion molecule (MSCRAMM) and that we have shown how the BR187–385 structure is involved in the binding of KRT10 and the formation of biofilms by S. pneumoniae.
the KRT10 binding site of PsrP is formed by two distinct, but structurally linked binding surfaces, and that this is a unique structural feature among known MSCRAMMs.

BR187–385 of PsrP adopts a variant of the DE-IgG fold with a basic groove that is likely to interact with the acidic helical domain of KRT 10, and that the other side of its barrel is important for interaction with KTR10.
The main takeaway from our work is that

BR187–385 is a new member of the family of MSCRAMM adhesins, which are characterized by the DEv-Igg fold, despite the low sequence identity and the absence of the canonical divalent metal ion-binding site.
the KRT10-recognizing BR187–385 domain of PsrP is a novel variant of a widespread bacterial adhesin fold.
the BR187–385 fold, despite low sequence identity, shares a common ancestry with the MSCRAMM fold, and thus represents a new member of this family.
